title: perf(objectql): memoize the cascade-delete closure on the registry object revision

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:「删除时会连带删掉哪些对象」这份清单,以前每读一个对象就把全部对象扫一遍重算;现在按对象注册表的版本号记住,版本号不变就直接给答案。
- 为什么改:控制台每次打开应用都要读整包元数据,包里每个对象都重算一次这份清单。Setup 包重复请求的 meta 中位数从约 184 ms 降到约 147 ms,隔一分钟再开从约 464 ms 降到约 356 ms。
- 风险与回滚:只有一种风险,就是对象变了而版本号没动、清单变旧;已核对注册表里每个让对象缓存失效的地方都会推进版本号。回滚就是撤掉这一个 PR,行为回到每次重算。
- 先看:`packages/objectql/src/engine-references-and-master-detail.ts` 末尾的 `getCascadeDeleteObjects` 与 `cascadeDeleteObjectsMemo` 说明块;`packages/objectql/src/engine-cascade-delete-objects.test.ts` 末尾新增的 describe。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/engine-cascade-delete-objects.test.ts`,预期 14 个测试全绿。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

`ObjectQL#getCascadeDeleteObjects` (the objects a delete of a record can cascade into, which the metadata read serves beside every `object` item as `cascadeDeleteObjects`) is memoized per engine on the schema registry's existing `objectRevision`.

- Key: the object name as asked, inside one memo per engine stamped with the revision it was filled at. A moved revision replaces the whole memo. A registry without the counter (a test double) declines the memo and every call computes, as before.
- Value: the computed list, frozen; every call returns its own copy, so a caller that edits its list cannot change the next caller's answer.
- A name the registry does not hold answers `undefined` and is not remembered, so the memo grows with the registered objects and never with what callers ask.
- Only `packages/objectql/src/engine-references-and-master-detail.ts` changes in the runtime. The rule (`collectCascadeDeleteObjects`, `cascadeRelationsInto`, `cascadeRelationBehavior`) is untouched, and so is the delete walk, which still reads the rule fresh.

## Why

The card's profile and the earlier report (6919782135) put the closure at about 47 ms of a Setup bundle call: an app bundle reads every object it names, and each read walked every registered object. The walk reads the registered object set and nothing else, and the registry already keeps a counter that moves on every change to that set, which the roll-up summary index and the record-currency parent lock already key on.

### Closure inputs, re-verified on 9e6fee19 before the first edit

- `resolveObjectName` and `getObject` read the registry's object index (`resolveObjectKey`, `resolveObject`); `getAllObjects` reads the merged objects.
- `cascadeRelationBehavior` reads one field definition (`statesDeleteSemantics`, `deleteWalkTargetOf`), resolves its target through the same index, and asks `isFederatedUnprovisionedInjectedColumn`, which reads only the schema it is handed (`isFederatedObject` and `resolveInjectedColumnProvenance` are pure functions of the definition).
- Package enablement reaches the merged objects only through the fold (`withholdDisabledExtensions`), and `enablePackage` / `disablePackage` both call `invalidateAll`, which moves the revision.
- Every site that drops the registry's merged-object cache moves `objectRevision`: `registerObject`, `unregisterObject`, `unregisterObjectsByPackage`, `removeObjectOverlay`, `withdrawObjectExtension`, `invalidate`, `invalidateAll`, `reset`. The refused-registration restore (`noteObjectEntry`'s restore closure) drops the cache without a bump itself, but its only caller, `restoringOnRefusal`, runs it inside a synchronous registration and calls `invalidateAll` right after `point.restore()`, so the revision moves there too. The earlier report's note on that restore is answered by this.
- No row, no caller context, no datasource posture and no per-call option feeds it.

## Tests

Seven pins in `packages/objectql/src/engine-cascade-delete-objects.test.ts`, a new top-level `describe` in the closure's existing harness file:

- a second call at the same revision does no walk (`cascadeRelationBehavior` spy not called) and answers the same list;
- invalidation: registering a cascading child moves the revision and the next call names it; unregistering one drops it;
- control: a registry change that leaves the object revision alone (a `view` item) keeps the memo (no walk) and the answer stays right, with non-vacuity asserts that the view landed and the counter did not move;
- cached equals uncached for every fixture object plus an unregistered name, the uncached reading taken through the same facet over a registry whose counter is hidden;
- each call gets its own copy;
- an unregistered name answers `undefined`, and its later registration is answered.

Ablations (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, each restored to the HEAD blob `ba03b08f`, `git diff HEAD` empty after each):

| mutation | red pins |
|:--|:--|
| never invalidate (`memo.revision !== revision` dropped from the refill test) | 3: both invalidation pins and the existing protocol pin "an object registered later ... is on the next read" |
| no memo (the lookup always misses) | 2: the second-call pin and the control |
| no copy (the frozen list returned as is) | 1: the copy pin |

## Acceptance notes

- Readings for the card's three cases plus first call, below. The Setup bundle moves; the showcase app bundle (few objects) does not move beyond noise, which is what a per-object saving predicts.
- The "reload more than one minute later" case is still dominated by the expired overlay row cache (about 219 queries, `db` 65 to 87 ms) and the full recompile; that is the shared compile cache's job (the third change), not this one.
- Not measured: hosted staging; cloud#4563 acceptance 1 is judged there.
